newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: British minister cuts short Gulf visit to vote.
newsitem.headline: British minister cuts short Gulf visit to vote.

text.p: Britain's junior Foreign Office Minister Jeremy Hanley said on Sunday he was cutting short a Gulf trip to return to London in time for a key parliamentary vote.
Hanley told a news conference in the United Arab Emirates that he would not attend an annual meeting of Gulf Arab and European Union countries due to be held in Qatar on Monday.

"I have been working hard to make sure I can attend the GCC-EU meeting in Doha...But unfortunately...I have been required to return to London to vote on Monday night," Hanley told a news conference in Abu Dhbai.
He said Britain would be represented by a Foreign Office official at the talks.

Britain's trade with the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states rose by more than 20 percent in the first 11 months of 1996 to 5.93 billion sterling on the same period in 1995. The GCC groups the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain.

The vote was called by the opposition Labour Party over Agricultre Minister Douglas Hogg's handling of "mad cow" disease. Prime Minister John Major's Conservative administration needs all available hands present for the vote, which is likely to be close.
